verses.1:1: Jude, a bondservant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James, to the called who are beloved in God the Father and preserved for Jesus Christ:
verses.1:2: May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied for you.
verses.1:3: Beloved, while making all diligence to write to you concerning our common salvation, I felt compelled to write to you, exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith delivered once for all to the saints.
verses.1:4: For certain men have crept in stealthily, who long ago were designated beforehand for this judgment—ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into licentiousness and denying our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
verses.1:5: Now I desire to remind you, although you once for all know all things, that Jesus, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe;
verses.1:6: and the angels who did not keep their own domain, but forsook their proper dwelling place, He has kept in eternal chains under gloom for the judgment of the great day;
verses.1:7: just as Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, having in like manner with these given themselves over to fornication and gone after strange flesh, are set forth as an example, undergoing the punishment of eternal fire.
verses.1:8: Yet in the same way these men also, in their dreaming, defile the flesh, reject dominion, and revile glorious ones.
verses.1:9: Yet Michael the archangel, when he was contending with the devil and disputing concerning the body of Moses, did not dare to pronounce a reviling judgment, but said, "The Lord rebuke you!"
verses.1:10: But these men revile whatever things they do not know; and whatever things they understand by instinct, like unreasoning beasts, in these things they are destroyed.
verses.1:11: Woe to them! For they have walked in the way of Cain, abandoned themselves to the error of Balaam for gain, and perished in the rebellion of Korah.
verses.1:12: These are hidden reefs in your love feasts as they feast together, shepherding themselves without fear; waterless clouds carried along by winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted;
verses.1:13: wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shameful deeds; wandering stars, for whom the gloom of darkness has been kept forever.
verses.1:14: Now Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied about these men, saying, "Behold, the Lord came with His holy ten thousands,
verses.1:15: to execute judgment upon all, and to convict all the ungodly concerning all their deeds of ungodliness which they have committed in an ungodly way, and concerning all the harsh things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him."
verses.1:16: These are murmurers, faultfinders, walking according to their own lusts; and their mouth speaks boastful words, flattering people for the sake of advantage.
verses.1:17: But you, beloved, call to mind the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.1:18: how they used to say to you, "In the last time there shall be mockers, walking after their own ungodly lusts."
verses.1:19: These are those who create divisions, merely natural, not having the Spirit.
verses.1:20: Yet you, beloved, building yourselves up upon your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit,
verses.1:21: keep yourselves in the love of God, awaiting the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ leading to eternal life.
verses.1:22: And show mercy to some who are doubting;
verses.1:23: save others, snatching them out of the fire; and show mercy to still others with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh.
verses.1:24: Now to Him who is able to guard you from stumbling and to present you unblemished before His glory with exultant joy,
verses.1:25: to the only God, our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, might, and authority, before every age, and now, and throughout all ages. Amen.

notes.1:5: The Greek critical text reads "Jesus" rather than "the Lord" or "God" found in some manuscripts, identifying the preexistent Christ as the one who delivered Israel out of Egypt.
notes.1:12: The Greek word translated "hidden reefs" can also mean "blemishes" or "spots," a resonance that fits both the surrounding maritime imagery and the parallel in 2 Peter 2:13.
notes.1:14: Jude cites a prophecy attributed to Enoch (cf. 1 Enoch 1:9); the Greek phrase "His holy ten thousands" literally refers to the Lord's vast host of angelic holy ones.
notes.1:22: Verses 22-23 follow the three-clause reading of the earliest Greek manuscripts, distinguishing three groups needing pastoral care, whereas later manuscripts preserve a shorter two-clause form.
